target_customer: Casual users who organize notes, pictures, people and places on iPad and iPhone
problem: Spreadsheets and note apps were built for mouse and keyboard, not for touch and visual planning.

competitors.name: Microsoft Excel
competitors.what: Dominant spreadsheet, power user oriented, with touch Office apps coming

technical_complexity.rationale: Real time collaboration and a touch gesture input system on iOS in 2012 were hard for three people.

defensibility.rationale: TechCrunch and reviewers saw Grid as closer to a scrapbook than a spreadsheet, which larger note apps could copy.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No acquisition found; Crunchbase and CB Insights list the company as closed.

market_need_then: Reviews in 2012 questioned whether Grid was a spreadsheet at all, as it lacked formulas at launch; demand evidence is limited to seed investor interest.

brand_strength.rationale: Generic name shared with many products; the YC slug binary-thumb comes from the company name Binary Thumb. No brand coverage found.

pivots.to: Grid, a grid based productivity app for notes, lists and collages
pivots.why: Per 2013 review, calculation features were not the focus; not stated by the company

outcome_analysis: Grid launched a touch spreadsheet in August 2012 and announced a seed round in July 2013 from prominent angels and General Catalyst, amount undisclosed. Reviews called it a scrapbook rather than a spreadsheet, and Crunchbase lists the company as closed, but no shutdown account was found so the cause is not public.
notes: YC record has no website or description; the company is Binary Thumb, maker of Grid. Seed date 2013-07 is from CB Insights (30 July 2013); TechCrunch says Leong raised it shortly after YC S12 and announced it later. Amount not disclosed. YC lists San Francisco while another source says Mountain View. Shutdown date and cause not public. Funding coverage partial because the amount is unknown. Education not found.
